explanation:
The rate of radiation energy emitted by a body of surface area A, emissivity e, and kept at an absolute temperature T is given by Stefan's law

dQe/dt = eAT4,

where is Stefan's constant. If this body is kept at a surrounding temperature T0 then rate of radiation energy absorbed by the body is

dQa/dt = eAT.

Thus, the net rate of energy loss by the body is

.

If surrounding temperature is reduced by T0 (<< T0) then net rate of energy lost by the body becomes

.

Thus, decrease in the surrounding temperature increases the rate of energy loss by . To maintain the body temperature, the human being needs to increase the rate of energy generation (through chemical reactions in the body) by to balance the increase in rate of energy loss.

The human beings can also maintain the body temperature (without increasing the rate of energy generation) by reducing the surface area (e.g., by curling up) of their body. If surrounding temperature is reduced by T0 and surface area of the body is reduced by A (<< A) then net rate of energy loss by the body becomes

.

Thus, the rate of energy loss by radiation remains same if reduction in surface area is

,

where, the body temperature is .

We assume body to be black i.e., e = 1. The amount of energy emitted by the body in one second is

J.

The amount of energy lost by the body in one second is
